QUIC client test that reads base64 transactions from stdin and sends them over a stream.

# Purpose
This file defines a QUIC client test program. It creates a `fd_quic_t` instance, opens a UDP socket, and connects to a fixed IPv4 destination address and port. The program reads base64 encoded transaction data from `stdin`, decodes each line into a packet buffer, and sends each decoded buffer on a new QUIC stream with the `FIN` flag set. The main loop services the QUIC state machine and the UDP socket, creates a connection when needed, waits for the connection to reach the active state, and then sends one transaction per stream.

The file also defines the callback functions used by the QUIC stack to track connection and stream events. [`cb_conn_new`](<#cb_conn_new>), [`cb_conn_handshake_complete`](<#cb_conn_handshake_complete>), and [`cb_conn_final`](<#cb_conn_final>) update global state so the test can manage the connection life cycle. [`cb_stream_notify`](<#cb_stream_notify>) counts successful stream completions and logs stream failures. The [`main`](<#main>) function sets up workspace memory, configures QUIC limits and client settings, starts the client run, and then shuts down the QUIC instance and workspace after the connection closes.
